result.description: SHINING PEARL PTY LTD  Shining Pearl Pty Ltd is seeking an experienced Construction Estimator to join its growing team in Victoria. This role is responsible for assessing property damage, preparing accurate estimates, coordinating restoration works, and ensuring projects are delivered efficiently, safely, and to the highest quality standards.   Benefits  Salary plus Superannuation   Task & responsibilities   Conduct detailed on-site inspections to assess fire, water, mould, storm, and other property damage.  Evaluate damage in accordance with construction plans, Australian Standards, building regulations, and relevant codes of practice.  Prepare comprehensive cost estimates, quotations, scopes of work, and restoration reports for residential and commercial projects.  Calculate labour, material, plant, equipment, subcontractor, and overhead costs to develop accurate project budgets.  Estimate project durations, resource requirements, and completion schedules.  Interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, specifications, and insurance documentation to determine project requirements.  Coordinate restoration projects from commencement through to completion, ensuring works are delivered within approved budgets and timeframes.  Monitor project progress and conduct site inspections to verify quality, compliance, and contract requirements.  Liaise with clients, insurance representatives, project coordinators, contractors, suppliers, and trades throughout project delivery.  Source materials and services, obtain supplier quotations, and negotiate competitive pricing and delivery schedules.  Prepare tender submissions, variation estimates, progress claims, and supporting documentation where required.    Identify project risks, recommend practical restoration solutions, and implement cost-effective strategies without compromising quality.  Maintain accurate project records, cost reports, estimating databases, and documentation using estimating software and Microsoft Office applications.  Ensure compliance with Workplace Health and Safety legislation, environmental requirements, and company policies.  Deliver exceptional customer service by responding promptly and professionally to client enquiries and project-related concerns.  Travel to various project sites across Victoria and respond to emergency restoration call-outs as required.  Work independently while effectively collaborating with internal office staff and multidisciplinary project teams.  Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives to enhance estimating accuracy, operational efficiency, and client satisfaction    Qualification & experience   Diploma or Advanced Diploma of Building and Construction, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Estimating, or a closely related discipline.  At least 1-2 years of experience as a Construction Estimator or in a similar role.  Driver's license  Strong understanding of residential and commercial construction methods, building materials, and restoration practices.  Experience estimating insurance repair, restoration, or construction projects is highly regarded.  Strong communication, negotiation, organisational, and stakeholder management skills.  Ability to prioritise multiple projects and work autonomously in a fast-paced environment.   About Company     Shining Pearl Pty Ltd is a cleaning and restoration company that delivers a comprehensive range of commercial and residential cleaning services. The company also specializes in restoration estimation, cleaning, and project management, supporting clients whose properties have been affected by floods, fires, water intrusion, smoke, storms, and other emergency events. Its services include preparing restoration estimates and coordinating construction-related projects to help restore damaged homes efficiently and effectively       Work Type:  Full time   Salary:  $79500-79500   Job Publish:  06-07-2026   Job Expire:  05-08-2026   Apply Link:  https://workinitiatives.com.au/job/details?id=5990094   This job is brought to you by workinitiatives.com.au.

Product Development Technologist  
 This is a unique opportunity to join a leading Australian contract manufacturer within the health and wellness industry, renowned for developing premium nutraceutical, complementary medicine and nutrition products for both domestic and international markets. 
 If you're passionate about developing innovative health products and have the technical expertise to transform concepts into commercially successful products, this is an excellent opportunity to join a business at the forefront of nutraceutical manufacturing. 
  The Opportunity  
 Reporting into the senior leadership team, you will lead the end-to-end development of nutraceutical gummy and pastille products, from concept and formulation through to pilot trials, scale-up and commercial production. Working closely with Manufacturing, Quality and Regulatory teams, you'll ensure products are technically robust, commercially viable and compliant with Australian and international standards. 
  Key Responsibilities  
 
 Lead formulation and development of nutraceutical gummies and pastilles containing vitamins, minerals, botanicals, collagen, probiotics and specialty ingredients. 
 Develop and optimise formulations for texture, flavour, stability, shelf life and active ingredient performance. 
 Plan and execute laboratory and pilot-scale trials before transferring products into full commercial manufacturing. 
 Optimise manufacturing processes to improve efficiency, yield, quality and product consistency. 
 Troubleshoot technical and production issues through root cause analysis and continuous improvement initiatives. 
 Work closely with Quality and Regulatory teams to ensure compliance with TGA, FSANZ, cGMP and HACCP requirements. 
 Prepare technical documentation to support product registration, stability studies and regulatory submissions. 
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver innovative products from concept through to launch. 
 
  About You  
 To be successful in this role, you will have: 
 
 Bachelor's degree in Food Technology, Pharmaceutical Science, Chemical Engineering or a related discipline. 
 5+ years' experience in nutraceutical, food or pharmaceutical product development. 
 Proven experience developing gummy, pastille or other confectionery-based delivery systems. 
 Strong knowledge of ingredient functionality, gelling systems, encapsulation techniques and formulation science. 
 Experience managing products through pilot trials, scale-up and commercial manufacturing. 
 Solid understanding of Australian regulatory requirements including TGA and FSANZ, with exposure to international regulations highly regarded. 
 Excellent problem-solving, project management and stakeholder engagement skills. 
 
  Why Apply?  
 
 Join a well-established Australian manufacturer experiencing significant growth. 
 Work on innovative, science-backed health and wellness products. 
 Be part of a collaborative, technically driven team where your expertise will directly influence new product innovation. 
 Long-term career development within a business investing heavily in research, manufacturing and continuous improvement. 
 Competitive salary package, supportive leadership and genuine opportunities to make an impact. 
 
 If you're an experienced Product Development Technologist looking to take ownership of innovative nutraceutical product development in a growing organisation, we'd love to hear from you. 
 Apply now or contact  lauren.duignan@persolapac.com  at PERSOL for a confidential discussion. 


 Please  click here  to apply.

You will perform highly skilled technical duties involving installation, advanced fault diagnosing, testing, repairing, servicing, precise calibration of complex and a wide range of electronic equipment and household electrical appliances including televisions, audiovisual equipment, display devices, home entertainment systems, security cameras, microwave ovens, refrigerators, washing machines, coffee machines, air fryer and other electronic products. Trainee - General Medicine

Orange Health Service

This position offers 12 months unaccredited experience in Medical Oncology and Radiation Oncology.

The main role is to provide clinical care to medical oncology and radiation oncology inpatients and outpatients under the supervision of Staff Specialists. The Advanced Trainee will work as part of a multidisciplinary team and supervise junior medical officers (JMOs) and medical students. It is also expected that the Advanced Trainee participates in the clinical meetings and teaching and be subject to training and performance reviews.

About Orange Hospital

Focusing on innovative models of care, Orange Health Service is the largest rural hospital in NSW and the regional teaching, referral and trauma centre for the Central West. The 520 bed campus has a 270 bed general hospital, with five operating suites and 60 specialised treatment areas.

Opened in 2011, services include FACEM-staffed emergency, inclusive of trauma; level 5 intensive care, medical, general and specialist surgical; obstetrics; paediatrics; level 4 maternity; dialysis; dental; cardiology, stroke, telestroke, interventional cardiology; radiation oncology; ambulatory care; rehabilitation; sub-acute-non-acute; diagnostic and a range of primary and community health services.

The hospital has one of the largest regional clinical trials units conducting a range of trials (incl tele trials and phase 1 trials) across a several specialties.

Our team provides high performing, harmonious care with a multitude of valuable training opportunities in a supportive and convivial environment. The scope, size and stability of the team, and our commitment to training and experiential learning, make it an ideal platform for trainee development. Special emphasis is placed on developing clinical autonomy, organisational skills, close working relationships with senior clinicians and where appropriate, supervision of junior trainees.

Orange Health Service is a teaching hospital associated with the University of Sydney and Charles Sturt University. There is an excellent record of success in college professional exams and also future placement with metropolitan hospital training programs.
And importantly, our supportive administrative team caters to trainees as individuals in their rostering schedules and career pathways, so it's no wonder Orange is well known for great trainee experiences.

About Orange

Just three and a half hours from Sydney and Canberra and home to nearly 70,000 people, the Orange Region is a unique appealing blend of a vibrant regional city, historic villages, abundant natural resources, scenic landscapes and established infrastructure.It's also a leading wine growing region with over 30 cellar doors all within 20 minutes from the city.

Imagine finishing your shift and heading to play an indoor team sport, hit the heights of a hiking trail, or take time out in a buzzing local pub - all just minutes from home. Orange offers the perfect fusion of laid-back regional living and sophisticated city culture.

 Wine & Dine Capital: Home to some of Australia's most awarded cool-climate wineries and many restaurants.

 Nature on Your Doorstep: Surrounded by national parks, lakes, and bushwalking trails - ideal for weekend adventures.

 A Place to Belong: Great schools, vibrant arts and culture, and a strong sense of community.

 A lifestyle you can afford: Choose the lifestyle you want with real housing options and room to breathe.

Orange is the perfect place for those looking for excellent clinical training while still enjoying a good work life balance.Apply now!

Watch our video for the JMO Experience in Western NSW Local Health District.

.Country living with a meaningful career path

.Flexible work practices (as appropriate to the position and negotiated with your manager)

.Corporate wellbeing programs, including the Fitness Passport

.Opportunities for learning and development, including in-house training with My Health Learning and the NSW Health RTO

.Professional growth and accelerated career progression

Where you'll be working

You will be based at Orange Health Service, a part of the Western NSW Local Health District. For more information on living and working in our beautiful region, visit our website Orange | NSW Government

Helping you move to Western NSW

The Welcome Experience is a free NSW Government service supporting workers (and their families) who have accepted a job with Western NSW LHD in most locations. The service helps with housing, schooling, partner work and community connections. Find out more

.MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia in an appropriate registration category.

.Completion of at least three (3) postgraduate years of medical practice.

.Valid NSW Working with Children check.

.Cleared National Police check.

.Aged Care Check for Australian Government funded positions.

.To be employed by NSW Health you are required to provide evidence of vaccination to comply with the NSW Health Occupational Assessment, Screening & Vaccination against Specified Infectious Diseases Policy, this includes any amendments made from time to time.

.You must take all reasonable care for yourself and others and comply with any reasonable instruction, policies and procedures relating to work health safety and wellbeing.

 

To apply, please address the following Selection Criteria:

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role.

Successful completion of three post graduate years, with a minimum of 12 months experience working within the Australian public health care system within the previous 24 months

Demonstrated orientation to rural-regional practice through life experiences, medical school and-or residency, outlining evidence of commitment to the provision of health care in a rural setting, preferably with experience of rural or regional medicine.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team including leadership and direction to ensure appropriate management of patients.

Demonstrated ability to work independently within a supervised complex clinical environment utilising excellent clinical skills, judgement and expertise, with demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Ongoing Full-Time 

About the Role:

Lyell McEwin Hospital is one of South Australia's busiest public hospitals, and the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is growing to meet the needs of one of the state's fastest-expanding communities. If you thrive in a clinical environment and bring strong organisational skills to everything you do, this full-time, ongoing Unit Secretary role within the DSSA Division could be exactly the right next step.

What You'll Be Doing

Working at the heart of the DSSA Division at Lyell McEwin Health Service, you'll provide high-quality administrative and clerical support that keeps the unit running smoothly and allows clinical staff to focus on patient care.

Manage patient administrative processes including admissions, discharges, and medical record coordination

Provide reception and communication support, acting as a key point of contact for patients, families, and clinical teams

Coordinate scheduling, correspondence, and documentation to support divisional operations

Maintain accurate data entry and records in clinical and administrative systems in line with SA Health policy

What You Bring

Demonstrated experience in an administrative or secretarial role, ideally within a health or community services setting

Proficiency in Microsoft Office and the ability to learn health-specific systems such as EPAS or similar patient management platforms used across SA Health

Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate clearly and compassionately with patients and multidisciplinary teams

Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities in a busy environment

Understanding of, or willingness to learn, confidentiality obligations and clinical administrative standards within SA Health

Work performed will be under limited supervision from a certified tradesperson or supervisor and may require supervision of a Maintenance or Grounds Assistant. Work undertaken will be conducted to the highest standards of repair, presentation and hygiene.

Respond to maintenance requests in a timely manner with work undertaken to a high standard.
